analysis:
Integration of all 8 units. The PR is CI-only: .github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/docs-impact.yml, changelog.d/ci-git-swiftpm-cache.md, docs/developer/build.md, and two test scripts (scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py, scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py). No provider runtime, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), key custody, attestation or encrypted prefix-cache (T-041) code changes. T-041 covers the provider runtime cache, not CI caches.

Security-relevant behavior verified in the replayed patch text. action.yml gains a save-caches input defaulting to 'false', and the Swift build, SwiftPM repositories and Metal cache saves are all gated on inputs.save-caches == 'true'. Per the docs and the other analyses, ci.yml sets SAVE_CACHES only for push events on master or dev, so PR code cannot write caches that later trusted runs restore. This is a tightening compared with the base, where PRs could save scoped caches. The new SwiftPM repositories cache key is bound to OS, home layout, lane and the Package.resolved hash. Per the analyses, checkouts use persist-credentials: false, so the job token is not stored in the cached .git/config. A failed cached checkout falls back to deleting the workspace and checking out cold. Actions remain SHA-pinned. docs-impact.yml adds a blob:none filter and sparse-checkout excluding the evidence .gz and landing .mp4 files. Those changes are performance-only, and the job still checks out the PR head SHA as before.

The test scripts add assertions pinning the save policy, the checkout options and the single allowed continue-on-error on the cached checkout step. The relaxed continue-on-error checks go through the helper without_cached_checkout, which is only partially visible.

Remaining unverified: the head side of ci.yml was only partially visible (about 1200 lines of diff), and the 24 omitted replay units were not seen. Not confirmed: that every save step is gated on SAVE_CACHES, that release and signing workflows cannot restore a cache written by an untrusted ref, that a stale restored .git cannot affect provenance checks, and that the without_cached_checkout helper is narrow. The docs-impact.yml event trigger and token scope are pre-existing and not shown. No concrete regression is established.
